key_insight: Detonation-spraying conditions strongly control the trade-off between dense, hard self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings and their friction/wear performance.
engineering_relevance: The results provide process windows for restoring and strengthening machine parts with coatings that must balance low friction, wear resistance, and microstructural integrity.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lamellar coating structure, roughness, friction, wear rate, and hardness measurements, with best wear resistance at O/C = 1.856 and 1 s delay and maximum hardness up to 905.6 HV.
watch_item: Optimizing for lower friction can increase wear, so the process must be tuned for the intended service condition rather than a single metric.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
